subject: biology
title: PCR, electrophoresis and DNA profiling
key_idea: PCR makes millions of copies of a small DNA sample. Gel electrophoresis separates DNA fragments by length. Together they allow DNA profiling, which uses the pattern of fragments to identify individuals and show relationships.

blocks.text: PCR is an in vitro method that amplifies a chosen piece of DNA. It copies DNA in a machine, without using living cells.

items.meaning: A short single-stranded DNA sequence that is complementary to the start of the section to be copied.
A DNA polymerase from a heat-tolerant bacterium. It is not denatured by the high temperatures used in PCR.

blocks.text: The mixture contains the DNA sample, primers, Taq polymerase and free nucleotides. It is taken through repeated temperature cycles.

diagram.alt: The steps in one cycle of PCR.
diagram.prompt: Put the steps of one PCR cycle in order.
steps: Heat to about 95 °C: hydrogen bonds break and the DNA separates into single strands
Cool to about 55 °C: primers anneal to the complementary sequences at the ends
Heat to about 72 °C: Taq polymerase adds nucleotides to build new complementary strands
The cycle repeats, doubling the amount of DNA each time

items: The amount of DNA doubles with each cycle, so 30 cycles can give about a billion copies from one molecule.
Taq polymerase is used because it is not denatured at 95 °C, so it does not need to be added again each cycle.
The primers make sure that only the chosen section is copied.
PCR repeats three temperature steps: separate the strands, anneal primers, extend with Taq polymerase.
Each cycle doubles the DNA.

blocks.text: Gel electrophoresis separates DNA fragments, or proteins, by size. It works on charged molecules.

items: DNA fragments are cut with restriction enzymes or copied by PCR.
The samples are placed in wells at one end of a gel, in a buffer solution.
An electric current is passed through the gel. DNA is negatively charged because of its phosphate groups, so it moves towards the positive electrode.
Short fragments move through the gel faster and travel further. Long fragments travel less far.
The fragments form bands. DNA is made visible with a fluorescent stain or a radioactive or fluorescent probe.
Fragments of known length run alongside, so the size of unknown fragments can be estimated.

blocks.text: Proteins can also be separated by electrophoresis. The principle is the same, with separation by size and charge.

items: DNA moves to the positive electrode, and smaller fragments travel further.
Bands show the fragments present in each sample.

blocks.text: A genome contains many variable number tandem repeats (VNTRs), short sequences repeated different numbers of times. People differ in how many repeats they have.

items: DNA is extracted from a sample and the regions containing VNTRs are copied by PCR.
The fragments are separated by gel electrophoresis, making a pattern of bands called a DNA profile.
The probability of two individuals having the same VNTRs is very low. Identical twins are the exception.
Related people share some bands: each band in a child comes from the mother or the father.
More bands that match means a closer genetic relationship.
**Forensic science**: matching DNA from a crime scene to a suspect.
**Paternity and relationships**: showing who a child's parents are.
**Medical diagnosis and disease risk**: identifying alleles or repeat patterns linked to inherited disease.
**Animal and plant breeding**: checking parentage and finding genetic variability within a population, so that breeders avoid inbreeding.
A DNA profile is a pattern of bands from VNTRs, and it is highly specific to an individual.
Matching bands show shared ancestry, which makes profiling useful for identification and relationships.

checks.q: Explain why Taq polymerase is used in PCR.
checks.a: It is heat-tolerant, so it is not denatured at about 95 °C when the DNA strands are separated. It can therefore be used for many cycles without being replaced.

checks.q: Explain how gel electrophoresis separates DNA fragments.
checks.a: DNA is negatively charged, so it moves through the gel towards the positive electrode when a current is applied. Smaller fragments move faster and further, so the fragments separate into bands by size.

checks.q: A child's DNA profile has four bands. Two match the mother's and two match the man claimed to be the father. Explain what this suggests.
checks.a: Each band in the child comes from one parent. All four bands are accounted for by the mother and the man, so he is very likely the father.

items: Be ready to **interpret** a gel of DNA fragments: compare bands between samples and work out which individuals are related.
Genetic fingerprinting analyses DNA fragments that have been cloned by PCR.
It can be used to determine **genetic variability within a population**, as well as individual relationships.
DNA profiling is used to identify individuals and to work out genetic relationships between plants and animals.
PCR is used to amplify the DNA before the profile is made, because crime scene and other samples are often very small.
PCR is used to **clone** and amplify DNA: the identical copies are made in vitro.
Explain the role of each part: primers give a start point for DNA polymerase, free nucleotides are the building blocks, and Taq polymerase builds the new strands.
The gel is a mesh. Fragments of different lengths move at different rates, so they separate. A set of fragments of known length is run as a ladder to estimate sizes.
DNA profiling is used in forensics and for analysis of **disease risk**.
Electrophoresis is used for separating nucleic acid fragments or proteins.
You should be able to describe the practical method of electrophoresis.
